title: Kolmogorov-distance invariance estimate
statement:
There is a constant $K>0$ such that, for every $n,k\in\mathbb N$ with $1\le k$, every function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ of degree at most $k$ and variance exactly $1$, and every $\varepsilon\ge0$ for which all coordinate influences of $f$ are at most $\varepsilon$, the Kolmogorov distance between the law of $f$ on the uniform Boolean cube and the law of its Fourier--Walsh polynomial evaluated on independent standard Gaussian coordinates is at most
\[
Kk\,\varepsilon^{1/(4k+1)}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$
every coordinate influence of $f$ is at most $\varepsilon$
